narrative:
The model estimated a 61.8% probability that you would fail the bar exam on your first attempt. That means the model judged failure to be somewhat more likely than passing, and this risk estimate led to the denial of your law school application.

The strongest factor was your third-year class standing: you were in the second decile, while accepted students averaged around the sixth decile. This was the main reason the prediction leaned toward bar exam failure. The next most influential factor was your LSAT score of 35.50. Although it is slightly below the accepted-student average of 37.18, this factor actually worked in your favor and pushed the prediction toward passing. Your first-year standing, third decile versus an accepted average near the sixth decile, also pushed toward failure, but less strongly than your third-year standing.

Because this is a risk estimate rather than a certainty, you should ask admissions for human review and explain any context behind your academic record. Ask what specific evidence would strengthen a future application. Consider retaking the LSAT and taking additional coursework that demonstrates improved academic performance, then reapply once you can show stronger, more recent evidence.
